key_insight: An equal-weight 6H-SiC/h-BN composite withstands extreme oxidizing heat through protective surface-layer formation, porosity-mediated stress relief, and strengthened interfaces.
engineering_relevance: This lightweight, machinable ceramic is promising for structural components exposed to severe heating and thermal cycling.
method: Spark plasma sintering of equal-weight 6H-SiC and h-BN.
Oxygen-fuel torch testing in air and microstructural evaluation.
Finite-element thermal analysis and ReaxFF molecular dynamics.
evidence_signal: The composite survived prolonged heating and thermal cycling at surface temperatures above 1500 °C, while pure constituents rapidly fractured or eroded; thermal conductivity was unusually temperature-independent.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify exposure duration, cycle count, or retained mechanical strength, limiting assessment of service lifetime.
paper_title: SiC-BN composites with extreme thermal and environmental stability
